sections.title: Story
sections.narration: You feel an unbearable restlessness when sitting still. That sharp irritation is actually your brain reacting to empty time. In 2014, psychologist Timothy Wilson at Harvard University tested this on college students. The result? About 67 percent of men chose to shock themselves with electricity rather than sit alone with their thoughts for 15 minutes. Arthur Schopenhauer wrote about this exact pain in his Studies in Pessimism. He claimed human life swings like a pendulum between pain and boredom. Was he right? Later research confirmed that empty time actively triggers stress pathways. So why do we assume boredom is just laziness? It is not. It is an evolved warning system forcing action. In 2012, researchers at York University defined boredom as a distressing failure of attention. That's it. Schopenhauer saw the suffering, but modern science shows how to fix the focus. What happens when you try to escape it through constant noise instead? We cover that next. So next time you feel stuck, remember you feel an unbearable restlessness.

claims.claim: 67 percent of male participants chose to self-administer electric shocks rather than sit quietly alone with their thoughts for 6 to 15 minutes
Boredom is a distinct mental state defined as the distressing experience of wanting, but being unable, to engage satisfying activity
